sourcedFrom: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: A hammer-fired double-action/single-action .45 with an ambidextrous safety/decocking lever — so the strip begins with decocking, not with a trigger press. The Tactical is the FNX this book draws for its disassembly and lubrication figures, and it is the one variant with a thread protector to take off the muzzle before the takedown lever turns.

steps.title: Identify the Tactical: thread protector at the muzzle, optic on the slide
steps.action: Check what you have in front of you. The FNX-45 Tactical is the variant with a threaded muzzle carrying a screw-on thread protector, and it is the pistol the disassembly and lubrication figures in this book are drawn from. Confirm the pistol matches the illustrations before using this procedure.
steps.prose: FN states that this owner's manual was written exclusively for the FN FNX pistol, and inside that family it separates the FNX-45 Tactical out by name wherever the Tactical differs — the thread protector step, the lubrication diagram, the electronic-sight section and the specification table, which gives the Tactical an 8.64-inch overall length and a 5.3-inch barrel against the plain FNX-45's 7.87 and 4.5. The FNX-9 and FNX-40 share the mechanism but not those parts. If your pistol is not an FNX at all, this is the wrong book.
steps.quote: Unscrew the thread protector from the muzzle. (FNX™-45 Tactical only.)
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17 Cleaning and lubrication, Figure 18 caption, p.31

steps.title: Decock the hammer with the lever, then safety on
steps.action: If the hammer is cocked, decock it using the ambidextrous safety/decocking lever — press the lever fully down, all the way — and then place the safety in the on-safe position.
steps.prose: The FNX's lever does two jobs: pressed fully down it drops the hammer safely, and raised it blocks the mechanism. Fully is the operative word — a partial press leaves the hammer hanging between full cock and decocked, which is the worst place for it to be. Never lower this hammer by pulling the trigger and catching it with your thumb; FN forbids that outright, and on a .45 with a heavy hammer spring a slipped thumb is a discharge.
steps.quote: The decocking/“safety” lever has two functions, operating the manual “safety” and decocking the hammer.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §8 Operation of the ambidextrous safety/decocking lever, p.15
steps.warn: FN's rule: the hammer should only be lowered to the decocked position using the ambidextrous safety/decocking lever, never by pulling the trigger and lowering it with your thumb.

steps.title: Magazine out — pull the bottom plate if it hangs
steps.action: Press the ambidextrous magazine release and take the magazine out. If it does not drop free, pull gently on the bottom plate while you keep the release pressed.
steps.prose: A 15-round FNX-45 magazine is a tall column of .45 ACP and it is heavy; in a dry or fouled well it will sit rather than fall. The release works from either side, so use whichever thumb is on the gun. Take the magazine right out and set it aside before the slide is touched — with it still seated, racking the slide loads the pistol instead of clearing it.
steps.quote: Press the ambidextrous magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull gently on the bottom plate while pressing the ambidextrous magazine release.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §16.1 Unloading the pistol, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Chamber empty, and look at it
steps.action: With the magazine out, pull the slide back to eject any chambered round and lock the slide open on the ambidextrous slide stop. Then look into the chamber and confirm there is no cartridge in it.
steps.prose: The FNX carries a loaded chamber indicator, but the manual's own instruction is to look, because removing the magazine tells you nothing about the chamber. A .45 case sitting in the chamber mouth is large and obvious once you actually put your eye to the port — the mistake is not looking, not failing to see. Leave the slide locked open until you are ready to move on.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember that merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §16.1 Unloading the pistol, step 4, p.30

steps.title: Start the strip from a completely unloaded pistol
steps.action: Before disassembly, run the unloading procedure through to the end: hammer decocked, safety on safe, magazine out, chamber checked, magazines emptied.
steps.prose: FN's disassembly section opens by pointing back at the unloading section rather than repeating it, which is easy to skim past. It matters here because the next two steps put your hand around a slide under recoil-spring pressure while the muzzle is being handled — there is no room in that for an unresolved chamber. Do the whole sequence once, deliberately, and then commit to the strip.
steps.quote: Completely unload the pistol as described in Section 16.1.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 1, p.32

steps.title: Slide locked back on the ambidextrous stop
steps.action: Pull the slide fully rearward and lock it in that position by pressing the ambidextrous slide stop upward.
steps.prose: Full rearward, then the stop — the FNX slide stop will not catch on a half-retracted slide, and a slide that slips off it while your other hand is at the muzzle is how the thread protector step goes wrong. The stop is on both sides, so hold the pistol however lets your thumb reach it without losing your grip on the slide. This is the position the takedown lever needs to clear.
steps.quote: Pull the slide fully rearward and lock it into its rear position by pressing the ambidextrous slide stop upward.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 2, p.32

steps.title: Thread protector off — Tactical only
steps.action: Unscrew the thread protector from the threaded muzzle of the barrel and put it somewhere it will not roll away. This step exists only on the FNX-45 Tactical.
steps.prose: FN prints this instruction with the model qualifier attached, because a plain FNX-45, FNX-40 or FNX-9 has no threads and nothing to remove. Take it off before the lever turns: it stands proud of the slide, so it catches as the slide runs forward off the frame, and the threads underneath are where suppressed fouling and carbon collect out of reach of every other step. Put it back on whenever no suppressor or device is fitted.
steps.quote: Unscrew the thread protector on the end of the barrel (FNX-45 Tactic™al only) (Figure 18).
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 3, p.32

steps.title: Takedown lever ninety degrees clockwise
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever 90 degrees clockwise. It should turn under thumb pressure and stop cleanly at a right angle.
steps.prose: Ninety degrees on the FNX — a quarter turn, not the hundred the striker-fired FN 509 wants, and forcing it past its stop damages nothing but tells you the slide is not properly locked back. Keep the slide on the stop while you turn it. If the lever will not move, the slide has crept forward off the stop, which is the first thing to check before applying any more thumb.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 4, p.32

steps.title: Release the slide with a firm grip — it is under spring pressure
steps.action: Take a firm hold on the slide with one hand, then push down on the ambidextrous slide stop to release it. Keep hold: the slide is under the pressure of the recoil spring.
steps.prose: This is the moment the FNX can get away from you. Releasing the stop without a proper grip on the slide lets the recoil spring throw the whole assembly forward, and on a .45 that spring is not gentle. Wrap your hand over the top of the slide rather than pinching the serrations, and take the load before your thumb leaves the stop.
steps.quote: While holding the slide with one hand, release the slide by pushing downward on the ambidextrous slide stop. Be sure to have a firm grip on the slide as it is under pressure of the recoil spring.
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 5, p.33
steps.warn: Do not let the slide run forward on its own here — control it the whole way.

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame in one continuous movement
steps.action: Still holding the slide, let it return forward slowly and keep the movement going until the slide separates from the frame.
steps.prose: It is one motion, not two — the slide travels forward and simply keeps going off the front of the rails. There is no trigger press anywhere in the FNX strip, which is what the decocking lever bought you at the start. If the slide stops at the end of the rails, the takedown lever has rotated back; put it square again rather than pulling.
steps.quote: Still holding the slide, let it slowly return forward and continue this movement in order to separate the slide from the frame (Figure 20).
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 6, p.33

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down. Gently compress the recoil spring, release its rear end from the barrel lug and lift the spring up and out of the slide. Then grip the barrel by its lug and lift it up and out.
steps.prose: Compress first, release second — the rear of the spring is trapped on the barrel lug and pulling on it without taking the compression off just drags the spring against the slide. With the spring gone, the barrel lifts straight out of the slide; on the Tactical it is the long 5.3-inch tube with the threads at the front, so handle it by the lug and keep the threads off the bench. Three groups now: frame, slide, barrel, plus the spring and the thread protector.
steps.aside: FN's next instruction, for the barrel: Grip the barrel by its lug and then lift it up and out of the slide.
steps.quote: from the barrel lug and then lift the spring up and out of the slide (Figure 21).
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, step 8, p.33

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring and the Tactical's thread protector. FN states this is as far as the pistol comes apart for cleaning and that anything further belongs to an authorized armorer or the FN Product Service Center.
steps.prose: That gives you the bore and chamber, the breech face and extractor, the slide rails, the barrel's unlock surface and the frame's magazine well — the whole list the lubrication figure marks up, drawn on the Tactical. Note one FNX-specific point while everything is apart: the polymer frame does not require lubrication, so oil belongs on the metal bearing surfaces and nowhere else. The magazine strip and the backstrap change are the deeper procedures this book publishes.
steps.quote: Do not disassemble the pistol beyond this point. (FNX™-45 Tactical shown.)
steps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.1 Disassembling the pistol, Figure 23 caption, p.33

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart — it is meant to be routine on the FNX
deepSteps.action: Eject and completely unload the magazine. Press the protruding part of the magazine retainer through the hole in the bottom plate with a small screwdriver, hold it there and slide the bottom plate slightly forward. Then, holding the bottom catch against the spring's force, slide the plate off and release the spring carefully. Remove the spring, follower and retainer together.
deepSteps.prose: FN treats FNX magazine disassembly as part of normal maintenance rather than an exceptional job, and it takes seconds once the retainer is depressed. The bottom catch is directly under the magazine spring, so the plate goes forward under your thumb and the pressure comes off gradually — a released .45 magazine spring will throw the retainer clear across a room. Wear eye protection: FN's warning at the head of this section is specifically about spring-loaded parts.
deepSteps.aside: FN's framing for this job: Disassembling the magazine takes only a few seconds and should be a part of the pistol's normal maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the magazine spring together with the follower and retainer.
deepSteps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17.4 Disassembling the magazine, step 4, p.38

deepSteps.title: Backstrap swap with a 1/16" punch
deepSteps.action: With the pistol completely unloaded, the muzzle safe and the safety on, insert a 1/16" punch or similar small instrument into the hole in the backstrap and push gently inward to release the internal locking tab. Keep light pressure on the punch and slide the backstrap down off the grip; the replacement slides up the rail and snaps into place.
deepSteps.prose: The FNX ships with four backstraps, so this is a fitting job as much as a cleaning one — but it is also the only way to reach the channel underneath, where sweat and lint accumulate on a carried .45. Light pressure is the whole technique: the tab only needs to clear, and leaning on the punch marks the polymer. Check the replacement has snapped fully home by pulling on it before the pistol goes back together.
deepSteps.quote: Insert a 1/16" punch or other small instrument into the hole in the backstrap and gently push inward to release the internal locking tab (Figure 30).
deepSteps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §19.1 Interchangeable backstraps, step 1, p.40

deepSteps.title: The polymer frame takes no oil
deepSteps.action: When you lubricate, keep it to the metal bearing surfaces the lubrication figure marks — barrel unlock surface, slide rails, barrel exterior. Put no lubricant on the polymer frame itself.
deepSteps.prose: This is an FNX-specific instruction and it is easy to violate by habit, wiping an oily rag over the whole frame at the end of a clean. Oil on polymer does nothing useful and holds the grit that then works into the rails. FN pairs it with a blunt warning against excessive lubricant anywhere, because too much interferes with the functioning of the pistol — on a DA/SA .45 that shows up as a sluggish trigger return before it shows up as anything else.
deepSteps.quote: It is important to keep your pistol clean and correctly lubricated, however, the polymer frame of the FNX pistol does not require lubrication.
deepSteps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17 Cleaning and lubrication, p.31
deepSteps.warn: NOTICE! DO NOT USE EXCESSIVE LUBRICANT. USING TOO MUCH LUBRICANT CAN INTERFERE WITH THE FUNCTIONING OF YOUR PISTOL.

deepSteps.title: Solvents that damage an FNX
deepSteps.action: Choose your cleaning products before you start. Never soak the pistol in hydrocarbons, ammonia, trichloroethylene or Teflon-based lubricants.
deepSteps.prose: FN names these four specifically, and the reason is the mix of materials in an FNX — a polymer frame, a stainless barrel and coated steel parts do not all tolerate the same chemistry. Ammonia in particular is common in copper-fouling removers, which is exactly the bottle someone reaches for after a hard range session. Use the product on the bore, on a patch, for the time it needs, and do not park the pistol in a tray of anything.
deepSteps.aside: FN's list, from the same section: never soak your firearm in hydrocarbons, ammonia, trichloroethylene or Teflon-based lubricants as they can cause damage to your pistol.
deepSteps.quote: Clean and lubricate your pistol after every use or, in case of intensive shooting, every 500 rounds.
deepSteps.cite: FN FNX™ AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 1608 - FNX - OM 66-100028 — §17 Cleaning and lubrication, p.31

cleaning.name: BARREL, BORE & MUZZLE THREADS
tasks: Solvent into the bore and chamber of the 5.3-inch Tactical barrel, then rod and patches until they come out clean
Brush the muzzle threads and the shoulder behind them — with the thread protector off, this is the only time they are reachable
A lightly oiled patch through the bore afterwards for protection, wiped dry before the pistol is fired
Light oil on the outside of the barrel and its unlock surface

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & LUBRICATION POINTS
tasks: Brush and solvent on the breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port
Wipe the slide rails on both sides and lubricate the points the figure marks — the barrel unlock surface, the rails and the barrel
Nothing on the polymer frame: FN states it does not require lubrication
Soft cloth through the magazine well to clear debris

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & PUT-AWAY
tasks: Clean the magazine parts with a soft cloth, then a lightly lubricated cloth on the metal, wiping the excess off
Never soak the pistol in hydrocarbons, ammonia, trichloroethylene or Teflon-based lubricants
Clean after every use, or every 500 rounds in intensive shooting; dirty ammunition and suppressed shooting bring that forward
Wipe the outside down and store with the hammer decocked, the safety on safe and the chamber and magazine empty

reassembly: Reverse the strip: barrel into the slide first, muzzle forward through the barrel opening, seated on its lug.
Recoil spring back into the slide, its rear end engaged on the barrel lug, compressed as it goes in.
Slide and barrel onto the frame rails, run fully rearward and locked open on the ambidextrous slide stop.
Rotate the takedown lever back 90 degrees to lock frame and slide together, then release the slide forward under control.
Thread protector — or a suppressor or muzzle device rated for .45 ACP — back onto the muzzle threads, square and hand tight.
Decock the hammer with the ambidextrous lever, set the safety on safe, and function-test before loading.
fncheck: Empty and reassembled: the takedown lever should sit flush and refuse to turn against a closed slide; the slide should run into battery under its own spring and lock back on either side of the ambidextrous stop; raising the safety/decocking lever should cover the red warning dot and block the trigger, and pressing it fully down should drop the hammer cleanly to the decocked position; the first trigger pull from decocked should be long and heavy double-action, with subsequent pulls short and light single-action; an empty magazine should seat and drop free on either magazine release; and the thread protector should be square and tight on the Tactical's muzzle threads.
